start: Write an AppHost for our order system: PostgreSQL with the database orders, Redis, the API project Orders.Api, and the worker Orders.Worker. Start the API and the worker after the database is ready.
Our AppHost still uses Aspire.AppHost.Sdk 13.6.5 and AddProject<Projects.Api>. Move it to Aspire 17.
Write an integration test that starts the AppHost and checks that GET /health of the api resource returns 200.
Add RabbitMQ to the AppHost and let the worker get its connection from Aspire instead of appsettings.json.
Set up the Aspire MCP server for Claude Code so the agent can read the logs and traces of the running app.
skip: Write a docker-compose.yml that runs the API, PostgreSQL, and Redis for local development.
Write the Kubernetes Deployment and Service manifests for the order API by hand.
Add OpenTelemetry traces and metrics to the order API and export them to an OTLP collector. We do not use Aspire.
Add Dapr to the order service so it publishes events through the Dapr pub/sub building block.
Add a /healthz endpoint to this minimal API that checks the database connection.
